findings.title: strict-typing row reads done while manifest requirement threadpoolctl ships no py.typed and has no stub package
findings.claim: quality_scale.yaml marks strict-typing done, but one of the three manifest requirements, threadpoolctl, ships no py.typed (3.7.0 installed, 3.8.0 as pinned in tests/requirements-typing.txt) and has no types-/-stubs distribution, which the rule (no exceptions) and its hassfest check require.
findings.mechanism: The row's comment reads the rule's py.typed half as the integration's own marker (qs_py_typed_files=1), but the rule page says 'Its library must be typed as well, and ship a py.typed file' and hassfest checks 'every requirement in its manifest must ship a py.typed file, or have a separate types- stubs package'. optimizer.py:1447 itself records that threadpoolctl publishes no py.typed and no stub distribution exists, and resolves it by importlib to dodge import-untyped. tests/entities.py derives the manifest tier from these rows, so the manifest's quality_scale: platinum rests on the false row. Fails D10-criteria Q2.

findings.title: Coordinator has no config_entry: HeatPumpOptimizerConfigEntry annotation under a done strict-typing row
findings.claim: HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator (the integration's one DataUpdateCoordinator subclass) declares no config_entry annotation anywhere in its in-package MRO, so its config_entry is the base's bare ConfigEntry | None, while strict-typing is done and its comment claims every attribute annotation is typed.
findings.mechanism: The rule pages (strict-typing: 'use a typed config entry everywhere you get one'; runtime-data: 'A coordinator that gets the config entry should use the typed entry too: config_entry: MyConfigEntry', pylint home-assistant-coordinator-untyped-config-entry) ask for the class annotation. The coordinator receives the typed entry (coordinator.py:3514) and passes config_entry=entry (3536) but never re-annotates the attribute; coordinator.py:7022 then reads it through getattr(self, 'config_entry', None). The doc_claims census (qs_entry_param_bare) counts parameters, not this attribute. Fails D10-criteria Q2.
